summary: The Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2025 makes adjustments to how the federal bankruptcy system is funded and administered. It increases the compensation paid to Chapter 7 bankruptcy trustees, extends and adjusts certain Chapter 11 quarterly bankruptcy fees, and extends the terms of specified temporary bankruptcy judgeships across various districts.

affected_groups.effect: Receive increased compensation per case administered.
Subject to extended quarterly fees and higher fee percentages for large disbursements.
Have the terms of their temporary offices extended for an additional five years.

key_provisions: Increases compensation for Chapter 7 bankruptcy trustees by raising the trustee portion from $45 to $105, bringing total per-case compensation to $120.
Extends certain quarterly fees paid to the U.S. trustee in Chapter 11 cases for an additional five years, moving the expiration/sunset timeline to 2031.
Increases the Chapter 11 quarterly fee percentage for cases with large disbursements from 0.8 to 1.1, subject to limitations.
Extends temporary bankruptcy judgeships in various districts from 5 years to 10 years.
Specifies how bankruptcy filing and quarterly fees are deposited into various Treasury and U.S. Trustee system funds.
missing_information: Exact financial totals or projections of increased revenue from the fee adjustments.
Specific names of the judicial districts receiving the 10-year extensions for temporary bankruptcy judgeships.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Bankruptcy Administration Improvement Act of 2025 makes adjustments to how the federal bankruptcy system is funded and administered. It increases the compensation paid to Chapter 7 bankruptcy trustees, extends and adjusts certain Chapter 11 quarterly bankruptcy fees, and extends the terms of specified temporary bankruptcy judgeships across various districts.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation modifies the operational funding and judicial staffing of the federal bankruptcy system to maintain its self-funded status and adjust trustee pay for the first time in decades.
